title: MPTCP: Add support for MP_CAPABLE C Flag
description:
Interpret C Flag as described in section 3.1 RFC8684

Issue: https://github.com/multipath-tcp/mptcp_net-next/issues/190

notes.body:
Hi Rui,

thanks for your submission. Could you please amend your commit message so as to fix the typo (MPTPC -> MPTCP)?
Fixed, sorry about that.
The bit description differs a bit from RFC 8684 (that describes it as "Do not attempt to establish new subflows to the source address"). Should not we put the RFC text?

> Should not we put the RFC text?

Well yes, it was just to make the description shorter, but if we can have a longer text, that is probably better. I will then change it.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3890/diffs?diff_id=230343798&start_sha=a6e4066a90664797a69572c236b8438837e63e76#ecc33d9ca259b01be33fa710cd6cf581a15d868b_7704_7704)

This is still not the same text as the RFC, where you keep indicating that it takes into account the port. IMHO it would make sense to use the exact same wording as the RFC, no? If you think this is not relevant, then we can use a shorter string (I don't know MPTCP).

From the [RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8684#section-3.1):

> The third bit, labeled "C", is set to 1 to indicate
                 that the sender of this option will not accept
                 additional MPTCP subflows to the source address and
                 port, and therefore the receiver MUST NOT try to open
                 any additional subflows toward this address and port.

I can rephrase again but the port is clearly mentioned.

Edit: I just realized you quoted the text from section 7.3, and indeed the port is not mentioned in there, however, the text in 3.1 is the correct one.
changed title from **MPT{-P-}C: Add support for MP_CAPABLE C Flag** to **MPTC{+P+}: Add support for MP_CAPABLE C Flag**

@pquantin 

I changed the description to better reflect the RFC, I think now should be better.

Just a mall nit and then I promise I stop :)
Why do you have capital letters for Subflow, Address and Port? The specification does not seem to use this syntax.

Haha no worries. The reason for that it's me. I keep capitalizing words that don't need to, and I don't know why, it keeps happening. :sweat_smile: 

I will fix it.

The bitmask should be changed from 0x3E to 0x1E as bit 0x20 is now used for C flag

Should hf_tcp_option_mptcp_C_flag also added here? If not, then we need to split hf_tcp_option_mptcp_reserved_flag in hf_tcp_option_mptcp_reserved_v0_flag and hf_tcp_option_mptcp_reserved_v1_flag as the reserved bits would differ

That's a very good point, I missed the reserved flags.

This flag was not used for version 0, as stated in the [obsolete RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6824), therefore I don't think it makes sense to add it. So I think you're right and we need to distinguish the reserved flags between the two versions, I'll change it.
